item: The pre-check refusal sentence is defined once and the shipped JS reader is driven with it
summary: The routes and loaders that refuse before they build a request (eight HTTP 409 details, the four statistics fetchers, three catalogue loaders, two entity loaders, the ring loader and the mailbox import) each spelled network refused: airplane mode is engaged as a literal of their own; the one reader of the text in src/ is the Wikidata fetch button's pattern in app-insights.js, which takes the route's 409 status first and matches the sentence only for a message with no status; nothing tied the nineteen to that copy, and the R317 pin scans a different sentence. NETWORK_REFUSED now sits beside KILL_SWITCH_REFUSAL in fetch_verdict.py with the text unchanged; the nineteen sites say it by name and the six that continue it build on it with an f-string (an AST fold of the nineteen messages before and after is the same string for all of them, so no behaviour or UI changes). entities/items.py builds it where it raises, so importing the module still loads neither src.ingest nor requests. The R317 pin now folds + and f-string pieces, squeezes whitespace out of both sides for the new sentence, reads no exclusion list, counts the reads of the constant through every import alias (pinned at 19; a relative or re-exported import and a rebinding fail) and plants its detector cases, Python and non-Python, from the constant; the node run of the JS reader takes the constant as its input, so rewording the constant without the reader fails there. 13 mutant runs: 10 red, 3 controls green. A UI gap older than this change is recorded, not fixed: a job that ends in error after the switch engages prints job.error without calling the reader (a proposal for the OSM lane).
